# Committed transcript menu hit candidate (2026-10-26)

Isolated from approved icon source `958084fdb843aa6f20f3ef50dea4f754e1cbcdb5`. Not part of the .3 installer until separately reviewed and integrated. This is a bounded far-blank stale-hover correction, not full Rust hit geometry or native macOS acceptance.

## Source contract and remaining differences
Pinned Rust `299a32bc87fe3d4851bdb902d9c03dcf9bf99cac`, `crates/orbit-pi/src/transcript_view.rs`: `message_at` (475–489) chooses containment then strict Manhattan edge distance `<24`; right-click (833–868) captures that message without changing selection. Registered paint bounds are at 750–813. GPUI partial clipping equivalence is unproved. Rust code lines are separate registrations; pinned MyGo code Body groups up to 32 lines into one RichText. This candidate deliberately does not pretend those internal blank regions match. No font/gutter/renderer changes.

## API and lifecycle
Fixed-pin overlay replaces only `ui/runtime.go` and `ui/menu.go`, adds `ui/orbit_menu_hit.go` and its tests. `RegisterTextMenuTarget` associates an immutable application token with a row's selectable descendants. `Menu.TextMenuHit` reads the original pointer opening and committed visible geometry. `Menu.Collecting` exposes only the existing collect/chosen phase. Default unregistered menus and all input selection/caret code are unchanged. Registered transcript keyboard opening has no pointer target and is refused, rather than reusing hover. This is not a general keyboard context-menu implementation.

Registration is cleared on every build pass, committed only after layout/selectable collection, and drops non-visible, disabled/inert and removed List rows. Window, scope, frame and current-owner checks fail closed. Counts are capped at 1,024 target rows and 4,096 blocks per frame (overflow discards the frame, not partial authorization). Scope ancestry walks are capped at 64. Gap and coordinates must be finite; negative limits are rejected; zero cannot satisfy strict distance `<0`. Occlusion uses exactly one hit-chain walk at the nearest block's interior point; if that closest block is occluded, it fails closed without choosing a farther block. Ties retain the first block in committed selectable traversal order (no map iteration). This is conservative and is not GPUI clip/paint-z equivalence. Tokens share existing strings without copying, parsing or logging payloads.

Only one opening token is retained between event and collect. It is cleared before invoking the collect callback, even if callback returns empty or panics; unresolved host and Close also clear it. The existing application opening snapshot remains one string pair tied to its owner host and is replaced on opening/cleared on choice or owner removal. It is **not** claimed to be immediately released on native dismiss (there is no public dismiss callback). Cancel then blank clears the old app intent without emitting items; chosen dispatch retains the original immutable message/selection snapshot.

Canonical wrapper verifies upstream identity, baseline hashes, the exact four-file set, source/hash/kind/path and patch hash before creating temporary sources. Module cache is not modified. Existing composer, selection-retention and Review overlays compose without a path collision. Without this optional hit API the custom transcript menu refuses the hit; no stale-hover fallback is used.

## Evidence and honest failure history
Original actual App RED `/tmp/orbit-blank-menu-red-0449-v2.jsonl` measured a point 80 and 157.7 pixels from the two text blocks and copied FIRST_MESSAGE after opening on blank. The same unmodified assertion passes with this candidate (`TestMessageMenuMeasuredBlankDoesNotReusePreviousHover`). The earlier v1 fixture accidentally hit another paragraph and is not behavioral evidence.

A separate bare-toolkit selection diagnostic failed because default selection behavior clears a selected range on far right click. Its source/log are preserved outside the candidate (`/tmp/orbit-menu-blank-selection-diagnostic-0834.go`, `/tmp/orbit-menu-blank-selection-red-0834.jsonl`). It is not an actual Orbit regression: canonical App with existing selection-retention passes selected-text → blank, and selected-first → right-click-second preserves Copy Selection while Copy Message targets SECOND_MESSAGE. Consequently **no menuPress/menuRelease hook was added**. The first other-text fixture used wrong label `Copy` and failed; corrected actual label `Copy Selection` passes. Original failed logs retained.

Matrix includes strict 24 and diagonal limits, invalid gaps, original opening despite pointer movement, cancel/reopen, old owner and foreign window, Close, empty results, default/keyboard menus, clipped List eviction, disabled/hidden/occluded rows, target overflow/recovery, final multi-pass registration, panic release and direct Windows release-path exercise. Windows test exercises its unchanged helper on the current host, not a physical Windows UI. Actual App tests cover original RED, selection, cancellation, old-owner choices and same-owner streaming snapshots. Final exact package/test hitset and hashes are recorded separately; no full suite or hosted-native claim from these focused tests.

The archived toolkit patch uses zero context (`git apply --unidiff-zero`) to avoid nested-patch whitespace diagnostics; canonical builds use the separately hash-verified complete source texts. Production toolkit diff and final repository diff checks pass.

## Review hardening (08:51)
The first frozen candidate had an explicit defense gap: a corrupted/derived opening distance of NaN or negative infinity satisfied its comparison. The negative test is preserved at `/tmp/orbit-menu-geometry-red-0849.jsonl`. Public transform constructors check finite inputs, but the runtime's parent world multiplication can overflow from two legal finite Scaling(1e20) inputs; a safe test repeats that exact multiplication without painting or allocating a huge raster. This is not a claim that real Orbit data has produced such geometry. Registration now rejects nonfinite world coefficients, raw/clip/intersection rectangles and edge sums; resolution checks derived distance; the public query independently checks the stored distance.

A real mounted single registration with 4,096 Text blocks is retained; 4,097 fails closed. A synthetic committed-block pressure test orders 4,096 distances worst-first and counts exactly one hit-chain call (not a permissive elapsed-time threshold). The same bound applies when the nearest block is occluded, with no farther fallback. Equal-distance traversal order is stable across repeated queries. Scanning is O(blocks) plus at most one existing whole hit-chain walk; the API does not know the caller's maxGap until collection, so no hidden hardcoded 24 shortcut was added.
